newsitem.title: GERMANY: Harvest incomplete in eastern Germany.
newsitem.headline: Harvest incomplete in eastern Germany.

text.p: Farmers are still cutting grain from the 1996 harvest in the eastern German states of Saxony and Thuringia, officials said on Monday.
"The rains won't let up and the days are getting shorter -- there is still some grain left in the fields," a grain analyst at farm union DBV in Bonn said.
DBV last week said Saxony still had 15 percent left to harvest and Thuringia five percent.
The official said little had changed over the weekend.
Efforts focused on rye and wheat, but some oats, triticale and oilseeds also needed to be brought in.
Rains had made harvesting in the region very difficult.

Moisture contents in some areas were 20-30 percent, and farmers had to transport grain to drying facilities, sometimes over long distances when local plants were too busy, the eastern German farm price office ZMP in Berlin said.
Farmers were marketing grain earmarked for bread making as feed because of quality losses, ZMP said.
Prices were steady as subdued local demand offset Polish buying.
DBV estimated additional operating costs for the 1996 harvest in Saxony at 200 million marks, adding that preparatory field work for winter sowings would also be costly and late.
Elsewhere in Germany, farmers had harvested a large crop of generally good quality, DBV said.
There was no shortage of wheat or rye for milling although only 80 percent of the rye crop qualified as bread rye versus 100 percent last year. Wheat protein counts were also good.
Farmers in most parts of the country were sowing winter rye and wheat, having finished barley and rapeseed, said an official at the DWD meteorological institute near Frankfurt.
"Cool temperatures are delaying winter rape growth, which is helpful because it makes plants more resistant, but the feed maize crop is ripening too slowly," he said.
"Cool and rainy weather has been beneficial for sugar content development in the beet harvest," he added.
DWD forcast maximum daytime temperatures of up to 12 degrees for Oct 2-10 after 11-18 degrees in the Sept 26-Oct 2 period.
The farm ministry estimate for the total national grain crop this year stands at 42 million tonnes, up 5.3 percent, with wheat at 18.9 million and rye at 4.2 million.
